comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
QUESTION 1 -- does rebar still use Success Criteria or Definition of Done?

Success Criteria: YES, live. Epic/container clarity scoring (gates.py:136 + its lockstep copy det_floor.py:227), plan-review criteria G3/G5/G7/COH/F1, the author guide (writing-a-passing-plan.md:58,76), the completion verifier (completion_verifier.md:59), and code-review scope extraction (assemble.py:253).

Definition of Done: NO, not a real concept. Only prose in a P1 failure message (det_floor.py:191) and a free-text synonym the completion verifier honours if an author happens to write one. The blocking floor across all types is '## Acceptance Criteria' with >=1 '- [ ]' item.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
QUESTION 2 -- will renaming SC->AC cause conflicts?

Found three, one expensive:
1. regver rotation. criteria_routing.json's check strings are hashed into registry_version(), which is bound into every signed manifest. Empirically confirmed a one-phrase edit rotates it: b058e30f0de6a907 -> 23913c1f6987711b. That read as stale-regver at the claim gate, invalidating attestations on 632 tickets (~40 open/in_progress).
2. Believed at the time to be a semantic merge, not a rename.
3. Epic clarity +2 becomes automatic since AC is already a universal floor.

CORRECTION made in the next turn: point 2 was wrong. Based it on the guide's PROSE. The criteria themselves pool the two everywhere -- F1 opens 'each acceptance/success criterion' with applies_at {suppress_types:[bug]} (no scope restriction, so containers too), G3 'each parent acceptance/success criterion', G7 fetches both as one contract. No criterion applies a different bar to SC. Altitude is carried by ROUTING (G3 applies_at scope:[container], firing on has-children), not by heading name. So the split is vestigial vocabulary and the guide prose is the actual defect.

Merging is also strictly TIGHTER: _count_ac_items counts '- [ ]' only under '## Acceptance Criteria', so SC criteria never reach the P1 floor and can never carry [operator-attested] (the verifier matches that token only on checkbox text).

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
WORK 1 -- grandfathering fix, ticket 1f32-f86e-8a51-4d8e (bug, class preexisting)

Operator ruled the stale-regver claim-gate rejection a bug: attestations valid at signing time stand as grandfathered. Implemented in compute_validity (attest.py): records non-blocking registry_drift {signed,current} and falls through instead of returning stale-regver; verdict retired. All other freshness dimensions still block. ADR 0053 written (amends ADR 0015); ADR 0015, plan-review-gate.md (both verdict lists + the currency rule), attest_gate.py and manifest.py docstrings updated.

KEY REGRESSION, caught by an existing test: removing the verdict silently OPENED the progressive drift-refresh REUSE path. attest.drift_refresh_candidate had relied on stale-regver implicitly to deny reuse on registry skew (the DRIFT_REFRESH profile skips the dep/head checks, so regver was its only guard). Caught by test_drift_refresh_skips_on_registry_skew. Fixed with an explicit registry_drift check. Seam now documented in ADR 0053: claim gate grandfathers, reuse path stays conservative.

Landed as Gerrit 962 -> merged 095c4afef (server-side rebase, so the local commit SHA differs; GitHub mirror lagged replication, which is why the first ff-only failed).

COMPLETION VERIFIER correctly refused the close on two criteria:
- A genuinely missing test. The AC demanded ONE test rotating the registry AND drifting a dependency, asserting stale-code. My test used an UNSCOPED attestation so it yielded stale-head -- a different path. Wrote test_regver_drift_does_not_mask_code_drift_on_a_scoped_attestation; landed as Gerrit 967.
- The gates AC. A ticket comment is inadmissible for a codebase-verifiable criterion. Retagged [operator-attested] (a gate RUN leaves no codebase artifact) and attested with the CI vote + exact tool output.
Ticket left OPEN pending 967's Verified +1.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
WORK 2 -- migration epic 1386-5e7c-391d-4a74 (tearful-cleansable-gopher), decomposed + plan-reviewed

Six vertical slices, expand -> migrate -> contract:
  S1 2aa6 reviewer prompts + criteria routing + regenerated guide   depends_on 1f32
  S2 35bc heading-detection code + its test corpus                  (no deps)  PASS/certified
  S3 93d0 eval specs, eval solver, gold-set expectations             depends_on S1
  S4 44c7 author guide + user docs                                   depends_on S1,S2
  S5 0a8c store migration, 108 tickets bullets -> checkboxes         depends_on S2
  S6 5f4d residual sweep + CI guard                                  depends_on S1..S5
Epic PASS/certified. S1 and S3-S6 blocked by unclosed deps, so not reviewable by design; no --force used.

GATE FINDINGS THAT CHANGED THE PLANS:
1. S1 asserted grandfathering was already in effect -- 962 had not merged. Now a real depends_on merge-order edge.
2. plan_review_T2.md:10 is a FALSE POSITIVE: 'stated success criteria for a trial' = pilot metrics, not the heading. Removed from S1 scope with an AC asserting the phrase survives. Same class as O-RAN-SC. This corrected the map given to the operator.
3. S2 planned to DROP the epic clarity bonus. Measured against the real _clarity_score: fixture goes 6 -> 4, below the default threshold 5 (RED), and every real epic in the store drops by 2. Changed to REPOINT the bonus to Acceptance Criteria: score-neutral at 6, no padding, no live regression across the 108 tickets being migrated.

PROCESS DEFECTS WORTH FIXING (not filed as tickets, pending operator's call):
- composer.py create-time file-impact warning keys on ticket TYPE while P9 keys on HAS-CHILDREN, so an epic is told 'the file-impact-coverage gate will otherwise flag it' when P9 can never flag a container. Its own comment claims lockstep with the gate; it is not.
- Following that warning, I set file_impact on the EPIC to stop whole-HEAD attestation staleness. This is a WORKAROUND, not canonical: P9 treats containers as legitimately having no file_impact, and the author guide scopes the nudge to leaves. Safe (child-change detection runs via relation_snapshot, not file deps) but should be reverted if the operator wants the epic canonical.
- A ticket-creation loop shifted all six story descriptions by one position; caught because a review finding quoted the wrong ticket's text. Verify description-to-ticket mapping after bulk creation.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
HANDOFF -- next actions, in order

1. Wait for Gerrit 967 (test(gate): pin that regver grandfathering cannot mask code drift) to get Verified +1, then Submit.
2. Fast-forward the worktree (../grandfather-regver) and close 1f32-f86e-8a51-4d8e with --class preexisting. The close precheck needs the merged rebar-ticket commit reachable from HEAD.
3. Closing 1f32 unblocks S1 (2aa6). Then: review-plan S1 -> claim -> implement -> land -> close.
4. Closing S1 unblocks S3 and S4-partially; closing S2 unblocks S4 and S5; S6 last.
5. Re-check epic and S2 currency with 'review-plan <id> --status' before claiming -- both are scoped, so unrelated landings should not stale them, but HEAD movement is worth verifying cheaply rather than assuming.

OPEN DECISIONS FOR THE OPERATOR:
- Whether to strip the epic's non-canonical file_impact.
- Whether to file the composer.py warning inconsistency as discovered_from work.
- The 'definition-of-done' / dod_uncertifiable vocabulary (verify_models.py:231, plan_review_verifier.md:81, plan_review_verifier_agentic.md:87) was deliberately left OUT of this epic's scope as a distinct concept.

NEVER-TOUCH LIST for the rename (false positives):
- O-RAN-SC (Linux Foundation telecom consortium): docs/adr/0021:13, 0022:13,21, 0023:13, .github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml:10
- plan_review_T2.md:10 'success criteria for a trial' (pilot metrics)
- tests/fixtures/jira/search.json, tests/fixtures/jira/comment_map.json (recorded records; one holds 'parent SC')
- Historical citations to a past ticket's numbered criterion: test_reducer_reduce_all.py:120, test_canonical_event_bytes.py:1, test_code_review_artifact.py:414
- src/rebar/llm/workflow/editor_assets/dist/editor.js (minified vendor bundle)
- Never run an unbounded case-insensitive 'sc' replace: the signed opcert envelopes in the store are base64.
